title: Caregivers' Knowledge of Emergency Department Discharge Instructions Improves With the Use of Video
brief_summary: Previous studies demonstrate that patients often have difficulty understanding their discharge instructions. Video discharge instructions have the potential to mitigate factors such as illiteracy and limited physician time, which may affect comprehension. Our goal is to determine if adding video discharge instructions affects caregivers' understanding of their child's emergency department (ED) visit, plan and follow-up.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* caregivers of pediatric patients age 29 days to 18 years old diagnosed with wheezing or asthma exacerbation, fever, or vomiting and/or diarrhea.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Caregivers of patients who were critical in the ED,
* Admitted to the hospital, or given an alternate diagnosis prior to discharge were excluded from the study.
* Also, non-English speaking caregivers were excluded.
condition: Evaluation of Video Discharge Instructions in Improving Understanding
